As of March 2026, four financial institutions in Guinea-Bissau are authorised to offer PI-SPI services, meaning the rails to support business payments exist, although actual uptake for B2B use cases in the country is likely still limited given the recent regional launch.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Given lack of data protection legislation, no statutory data breach notification requirements could be evidenced for Guinea‑Bissau; searched for breach notification obligations in Guinea‑Bissau law and regulator guidance.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check found conflicting signals. Two generic compliance-content sites (ANQA Compliance; Generis Legal Intelligence) assert a mandatory 72-hour breach notification requirement enforced by a 'National Cybersecurity Agency of Guinea-Bissau', but this reads as templated/boilerplate content reused across many country pages rather than a verified legal citation. By contrast, the specialised Data Protection Africa factsheet (an authoritative tracker) states plainly that Guinea-Bissau has NO data protection law and NO appointed Data Protection Authority, which is corroborated by a separate KYC/AML vendor site (Didit) also stating 'no comprehensive data protection law'. Given the direct contradiction between a specialist authoritative tracker and two low-quality generic compliance sites, the light check did not surface a genuinely authoritative confirmation of a mandatory breach notification regime, but the conflict is significant enough to warrant a closer look. Score kept at 0/Unknown; flagged for human review given the conflicting claims about a National Cybersecurity Agency and 72-hour rule that could not be independently verified.
revised_comments: No authoritative source confirms a statutory data breach notification requirement for payment service providers in Guinea-Bissau. The country has no comprehensive data protection law and no appointed Data Protection Authority, which would ordinarily be the vehicle for enforcing such a requirement.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No public PI‑SPI scheme rulebook or operating rules specific to retail instant payments found for Guinea‑Bissau; searched BCEAO PI‑SPI pages/press releases for “règlement”, “rulebook”, “manuel”, “operating rules”, and found only participant lists. (Note: STAR‑UEMOA operating rules exist publicly, but PI‑SPI rules not located.)
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light-path search surfaced BCEAO's official PI-SPI website, which was fetched and read in full. The row was moved to the full path. The site publicly and freely (no registration required) sets out core scheme rules: eligible participant types (banks, microfinance institutions, e-money issuers, payment establishments), the four client categories (individuals, business-persons, legal persons/businesses, public administration) each with distinct rules, the technical/monetary distinction between a 'transfer' (to an individual, up to 30 per calendar month) and a 'payment' (to a business/legal person/government, or transfers beyond the 30-per-month threshold), pricing (transfers between individuals are free), and a general assurance of compliance with international payment security standards. This is a materially fuller public disclosure than the 0/Unknown score assumed, and it applies to Guinea-Bissau as a UEMOA/PI-SPI member state. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Yes - Fully Public).
revised_comments: The BCEAO publishes the core operating rules of the regional PI-SPI instant payment scheme openly on its official website (pispi.bceao.int), covering eligible participant types, distinct client categories and their rules (individuals, businesses/legal persons, public administration), the technical distinction and monthly threshold between transfers and payments, pricing (free transfers between individuals), and a general commitment to international payment security standards. As Guinea-Bissau is a UEMOA member state within the PI-SPI scheme, these publicly available rules apply to the country.
